sampled_pages.title: Governance Commons | Sociotechnical Governance for Human–AI Systems

headings.text: Who authorized an AI agent to act—and how can you verify what happened?
What brings you to Governance Commons?
Describe the agent. Establish the boundaries. Preserve the evidence.
RFC-0001 is accepted; its new public boundary is not yet active.
Capability is not the same as legitimate authority.
Five public roles, not five equal standards.
Role, maturity, version, and baseline status stay visible.
Make a narrow claim that another person can inspect.
The public purpose is broader than the repositories.
A commons, not a regulator or certifier.

headings.text: Capability should never silently become authority.
A commons for governed human–AI systems.
Make authority, evidence, and recourse visible.
I began with questions, not credentials.
Build useful common ground without claiming the whole field.
Bring questions, criticism, experience, and craft.
A public project, not borrowed authority.
